definitions.gloss: 100 points; perfect score on a test
definitions.explanation: A score of 100 on an exam or test, representing a perfect result.
Used figuratively to describe something done perfectly or someone's ideal performance or qualities.

examples.japanese: {算数|さんすう}のテストで{百点|ひゃくてん}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: I got a perfect score on the math test.

examples.japanese: {百点|ひゃくてん}{満点|まんてん}のテストで{九十八点|きゅうじゅうはちてん}だった。
examples.english: I scored 98 on a test with a perfect score of 100.

examples.japanese: {娘|むすめ}が{初|はじ}めて{百点|ひゃくてん}を{取|と}ってきたので、{家族|かぞく}みんなで{喜|よろこ}んだ。
examples.english: Our daughter brought home her first perfect score, so the whole family celebrated.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}は{百点|ひゃくてん}だね。
{彼|かれ}の{対応|たいおう}は{百点|ひゃくてん}{満点|まんてん}だった。
examples.english: His handling of the situation was absolutely flawless.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{天気|てんき}は{行楽|こうらく}{日和|びより}として{百点|ひゃくてん}だ。
examples.english: Today's weather is perfect for an outing.

notes:
Composed of {百|ひゃく} (hundred) and {点|てん} (points). While the literal meaning is simply 100 points, the word carries strong positive connotations in Japanese culture, where school tests are typically graded out of 100.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百点|ひゃくてん}を{取|と}る: to get a perfect score
- {百点|ひゃくてん}{満点|まんてん}: a perfect 100 points; absolutely flawless
- {百点|ひゃくてん}のテスト: a test scored 100

USAGE:
The figurative sense is very common in casual conversation. {百点|ひゃくてん}{満点|まんてん} is a set phrase that intensifies the sense of perfection, used both literally and figuratively.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {満点|まんてん}: perfect score, full marks — more general; works with any scoring system
- {合格点|ごうかくてん}: passing grade — the minimum acceptable score
